questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A capacitor of capacitance 8$\mu$ F is fully charged by connecting it to a source of 200V. It is then disconnected from the supply and connected to an uncharged capacitor of capacitance 4$\mu$ F. The electrostatic energy lost in this sharing is:
questions.solution:
Given:

$C_1 = 8 \mu F = 8 \times 10^{-6}\ F$

$V_1 = 200\ V$

$C_2 = 4 \mu F = 4 \times 10^{-6}\ F$

$V_2 = 0\ V$

The loss of electrostatic energy when two capacitors are connected is given by:

$\Delta U = \dfrac{1}{2} \dfrac{C_1 C_2}{C_1 + C_2} (V_1 - V_2)^2$

Substituting the values:

$\Delta U = \dfrac{1}{2} \times \dfrac{8 \times 10^{-6} \times 4 \times 10^{-6}}{(8 + 4) \times 10^{-6}} \times (200 - 0)^2$

$\Delta U = \dfrac{1}{2} \times \dfrac{32 \times 10^{-12}}{12 \times 10^{-6}} \times 40000$

$\Delta U = \dfrac{16}{12} \times 10^{-6} \times 4 \times 10^4$

$\Delta U = \dfrac{4}{3} \times 4 \times 10^{-2}$

$\Delta U = \dfrac{16}{3} \times 10^{-2} = 5.33 \times 10^{-2}\ J$

Answer: $5.33 \times 10^{-2}\ J$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: What is the charge on $15\mu F$ in the circuit given?
questions.solution:
From the given circuit diagram, the $15\mu F$ and $30\mu F$ capacitors are connected in series.

The equivalent capacitance of this series branch is:
$C_s = \dfrac{15 \times 30}{15 + 30} = \dfrac{450}{45} = 10\mu F$

This series branch is connected directly across the $13\text{ V}$ battery. Therefore, the potential difference across the series combination is $13\text{ V}$.

The charge $Q$ on this series branch is given by:
$Q = C_s \times V = 10\mu F \times 13\text{ V} = 130\mu\text{C}$

In a series circuit, the charge on each capacitor is the same. Thus, the charge on the $15\mu F$ capacitor is equal to the total charge of the series branch, which is $130\mu\text{C}$.

Answer: $130\ \mu\text{C}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: In the given figure all the capacitors \($\mathrm{C}}_{1}, \mathrm{C}$}_{2}, $\mathrm{C}}_{3}\) and \( \mathrm{C}$}_{4}\) have the same capacitance \(4 \mu $\mathrm{F}$\). The emf of the cell is 12 V. What is the effective capacitance ?
questions.solution: The circuit consists of three parallel branches connected across the 12 V source. Let the left node be A and the right node be B.Branch 1 consists of capacitors $C_1$ and $C_2$ in series. Their equivalent capacitance $C_{12}$ is given by $\dfrac{1}{C_{12}} = \dfrac{1}{C_1} + \dfrac{1}{C_2} = \dfrac{1}{4} + \dfrac{1}{4} = \dfrac{2}{4} = \dfrac{1}{2}$. Thus, $C_{12} = 2 \mu F$.Branch 2 consists of capacitor $C_3$. Thus, $C_{branch2} = C_3 = 4 \mu F$.Branch 3 consists of capacitor $C_4$. Thus, $C_{branch3} = C_4 = 4 \mu F$.Since these three branches are connected in parallel between nodes A and B, the effective capacitance $C_{eff}$ is the sum of the capacitances of the individual branches:$C_{eff} = C_{12} + C_{branch2} + C_{branch3} = 2 \mu F + 4 \mu F + 4 \mu F = 10 \mu F$.Answer: \(C_{\text{eff }}=10 \mu \mathrm{ F}\)

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The space between the two plates of a parallel plate capacitor is fully filled with a conducting slab. Then the capacitance of the capacitor is :
options: Reduced to half of its original value
questions.solution:
The capacitance $C$ of a parallel plate capacitor with plate area $A$ and separation $d$ is given by $C = \dfrac{\epsilon_0 A}{d}$.

When a conducting slab of thickness $t$ is inserted between the plates, the new capacitance is given by $C' = \dfrac{\epsilon_0 A}{d - t + \dfrac{t}{K}}$, where $K$ is the dielectric constant of the material.

For a conducting slab, the dielectric constant $K$ is infinite, i.e., $K \to \infty$.

Substituting $K \to \infty$ into the formula, the term $\dfrac{t}{K}$ becomes zero.

Since the slab fully fills the space between the plates, the thickness of the slab $t$ is equal to the separation $d$.

Therefore, $C' = \dfrac{\epsilon_0 A}{d - d + 0} = \dfrac{\epsilon_0 A}{0}$.

As the denominator approaches zero, the capacitance $C'$ approaches infinity.

Answer: Infinite

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: By connecting two given capacitors, a technician was able to make two new capacitors having the effective capacitance $12.5 \mu \mathrm{F}$ and $2 \mu \mathrm{F}$. What would be the capacitance of the given capacitors?
questions.solution:
Let the capacitances of the two capacitors be $C_1$ and $C_2$.

When connected in parallel, the effective capacitance is $C_p = C_1 + C_2 = 12.5 \mu F$.

When connected in series, the effective capacitance is $C_s = \dfrac{C_1 C_2}{C_1 + C_2} = 2 \mu F$.

Substituting $C_1 + C_2 = 12.5$ into the series formula:

$\dfrac{C_1 C_2}{12.5} = 2 \Rightarrow C_1 C_2 = 25$.

We have the sum $S = C_1 + C_2 = 12.5$ and the product $P = C_1 C_2 = 25$. These are the roots of the quadratic equation $x^2 - Sx + P = 0$.

$x^2 - 12.5x + 25 = 0$.

Multiplying by 2 to clear decimals: $2x^2 - 25x + 50 = 0$.

Using the quadratic formula $x = \dfrac{-b \pm \sqrt{b^2 - 4ac}}{2a}$:

$x = \dfrac{25 \pm \sqrt{625 - 4(2)(50)}}{4} = \dfrac{25 \pm \sqrt{625 - 400}}{4} = \dfrac{25 \pm \sqrt{225}}{4} = \dfrac{25 \pm 15}{4}$.

The two roots are $x_1 = \dfrac{40}{4} = 10$ and $x_2 = \dfrac{10}{4} = 2.5$.

Thus, the capacitances are $10 \mu F$ and $2.5 \mu F$.

Answer: $10 \mu \mathrm{ F}$ and $2.5 \mu \mathrm{ F}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: When a dielectric slab of dielectric constant $\mathrm{k}=2$ is used to fill the space between the plates of a parallel plate capacitor, the capacitance of the capacitor is found to be $20 \mu \mathrm{F}$. What will be the capacitance when the slab is replaced with air?
questions.solution:
The capacitance of a parallel plate capacitor filled with a dielectric material is given by the formula $C = K C_0$, where $C$ is the capacitance with the dielectric, $K$ is the dielectric constant, and $C_0$ is the capacitance with air as the medium.

Given $C = 20 \mu F$ and $K = 2$, we substitute these values into the equation:

$20 \mu F = 2 \times C_0$

Solving for $C_0$:

$C_0 = \dfrac{20 \mu F}{2} = 10 \mu F$.

Answer: $10 \mu F$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A capacitor of capacitance $4 \mu \mathrm{ F}$ is charged to a potential of 24 V and then connected in parallel to an uncharged capacitor of capacitance $6 \mu \mathrm{ F}$. The final potential difference across each capacitor will be:
questions.solution:
The initial charge $Q$ on the capacitor of capacitance $C_1 = 4 \mu \text{F}$ charged to a potential $V_1 = 24 \text{V}$ is given by $Q = C_1 V_1$.

$Q = 4 \mu \text{F} \times 24 \text{V} = 96 \mu \text{C}$.

When this capacitor is connected in parallel to an uncharged capacitor of capacitance $C_2 = 6 \mu \text{F}$, the total charge $Q$ is redistributed between the two capacitors until they reach a common potential $V$.

The total capacitance of the parallel combination is $C_{eq} = C_1 + C_2 = 4 \mu \text{F} + 6 \mu \text{F} = 10 \mu \text{F}$.

Using the principle of conservation of charge, $Q = C_{eq} V$.

$96 \mu \text{C} = 10 \mu \text{F} \times V$.

$V = \dfrac{96 \mu \text{C}}{10 \mu \text{F}} = 9.6 \text{V}$.

Answer: 9.6 V

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q:
A network of capacitors is as shown below. If the voltage supply is 100 V , find the energy stored in the $6 \mu \mathrm{ F}$ capacitor.
$C_1=3 \mu F, C_2=6 \mu F, C_3=3 \mu F$ and $C_4=4 \mu F$
questions.solution:
The circuit consists of a capacitor $C_4$ in parallel with the series combination of $C_1, C_2,$ and $C_3$.

First, calculate the equivalent capacitance of the series branch containing $C_1, C_2,$ and $C_3$. Let this be $C_{series}$.

$\dfrac{1}{C_{series}} = \dfrac{1}{C_1} + \dfrac{1}{C_2} + \dfrac{1}{C_3} = \dfrac{1}{3} + \dfrac{1}{6} + \dfrac{1}{3} = \dfrac{2+1+2}{6} = \dfrac{5}{6} \mu F^{-1}$

$C_{series} = \dfrac{6}{5} = 1.2 \mu F$

The voltage across the series branch is equal to the supply voltage $V = 100 V$.

The charge $Q$ on the series branch is $Q = C_{series} \times V = 1.2 \mu F \times 100 V = 120 \mu C$.

Since $C_1, C_2,$ and $C_3$ are in series, they all carry the same charge $Q = 120 \mu C$.

The energy stored in the $C_2 = 6 \mu F$ capacitor is given by $U = \dfrac{Q^2}{2C_2}$.

$U = \dfrac{(120 \times 10^{-6})^2}{2 \times 6 \times 10^{-6}} = \dfrac{14400 \times 10^{-12}}{12 \times 10^{-6}} = 1200 \times 10^{-6} J = 1.2 \times 10^{-3} J = 1.2 mJ$.

Answer: 1.2 mJ

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Two capacitors $\mathrm{C}_1$ and $\mathrm{C}_2$ are charged to 100 V and 120 V respectively. It is found that upon connecting them together in parallel, the potential on each one of them is zero. Therefore
questions.solution:
Let the charges on the capacitors be $Q_1 = C_1 V_1$ and $Q_2 = C_2 V_2$. Given $V_1 = 100$ V and $V_2 = 120$ V, the charges are $Q_1 = 100 C_1$ and $Q_2 = 120 C_2$.

When the capacitors are connected in parallel, the total charge is conserved. If the final potential is zero, the total charge must be zero. This implies that the plates of opposite polarity were connected together.

The total charge is $Q_1 - Q_2 = 0$ or $Q_2 - Q_1 = 0$.

Substituting the values, $100 C_1 - 120 C_2 = 0$ or $120 C_2 - 100 C_1 = 0$.

This simplifies to $100 C_1 = 120 C_2$, which reduces to $5 C_1 = 6 C_2$.

Answer: $5 C_1=6 C_2$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A $5.80 \mu \mathrm{ F}$ parallel plate air capacitor has a plate separation of 5 mm and is charged to a potential difference of 400 V. The energy density in the region between the plates is
questions.solution:
The energy density in the region between the $plates is given by
\begin{aligned} \\ u & =\frac{1}{2} \varepsilon_0 E^2 \\ \\ & =\frac{1}{2} \varepsilon_0\left(\frac{V}{d}\right)^2 \quad\left(\because E=\frac{V}{d}\right) \\ \\ \Rightarrow \quad u & =\frac{1}{2} \times 8.85 \times 10^{-12} \times\left(\frac{400}{5 \times 10^{-3}}\right)^2 \\ \\ & =283.2 \times 10^{-12} \times 10^6 \\ \\ & =283.2 \times 10^{-6} \\ \\ & =2.83 \times 10^{-4} \mathrm{ J} / \mathrm{m}^3 \\ \end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A capacitor of $2 \mu \mathrm{ F}$ is charged as shown in the figure. When the switch $S$ is turned to position 2 , the percentage of its stored energy dissipated is
questions.solution:
Consider the given figure,
When the switch $Sis connected to $point 1, then initial energy stored in the capacitor can be given as
=$\frac{1}{2}$(2 \mu $\mathrm{ F}$) \times V^2$
When the switch $S$ is connected to point 2, energy dissipated on connection across $8 \mu $\mathrm{ F}$ will be
$\begin{aligned} \\ & =\frac{1}{2}\left(\frac{C_1 C_2}{C_1+C_1}\right), V^2=\frac{1}{2} \times \frac{2 \mu \mathrm{ F} \times 8 \mu \mathrm{ F}}{10 \mu \mathrm{ F}} \times V^2 \\ \\ & =\frac{1}{2} \times(1.6 \mu \mathrm{ F}) \times V^2 \\ \end{aligned}
Therefore, % loss$ of energy
=$\frac{1.6}{2}$ \times 100=80 \%

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The potential difference between the points $\mathrm{P}$ and $\mathrm{Q}$ of the arrangement shown in figure is
questions.solution:
Both battery positive terminals face left, so they oppose each other. Net EMF $= 28 - 14 = 14$ V (driven by 28V, counter-clockwise).

Capacitors in series: $C_{eq} = \dfrac{4 \times 8}{4+8} = \dfrac{32}{12} = \dfrac{8}{3}\ \mu F$

Charge: $Q = C_{eq} \times V_{net} = \dfrac{8}{3} \times 14 = \dfrac{112}{3}\ \mu C$

Voltage across $4\mu F$: $|V_P - V_Q| = \dfrac{Q}{C_1} = \dfrac{112/3}{4} = \dfrac{28}{3} \approx 9.33$ V

Since current flows counter-clockwise, positive charge accumulates at Q (bottom plate), making $V_Q > V_P$.

$V_P - V_Q = -9.33$ V

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The figure shows a network of five capacitors connected to a 20 V battery. Calculate the charge acquired by each 10 $\mu$ F capacitor.
questions.solution:
Left parallel pair: $C_{LT} = 15 + 5 = 20\ \mu F$

Right parallel pair: $C_{TR} = 10 + 10 = 20\ \mu F$

$C_{LT}$ and $C_{TR}$ are in series across 20 V. Since both are equal, voltage divides equally:

$V_{TR} = \dfrac{20}{2} = 10$ V across each $10\ \mu F$ capacitor.

$Q = CV = 10 \times 10^{-6} \times 10 = 100\ \mu C = 1 \times 10^{-4}$ C

questions.q: A parallel plate capacitor having a dielectric constant 5 and dielectric strength $10^6 \mathrm{ V} \mathrm{ m}^{-1}$ is to be designed with voltage rating of $2 \mathrm{ kV}$. The field should never exceed $10 \%$ of its dielectric strength. To have the capacitance of $60 \mathrm{ pF}$ the minimum area of the plates should be

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The capacitance of a parallel plate capacitor is $400 \mathrm{ pF}$. It is connected to an ac source of $100 \mathrm{ V}$ having an angular frequency $100 \mathrm{ rad s}^{-1}$. If the rms value of the current is $4 \mu \mathrm{A}$, the displacement current is:
questions.solution:
The displacement current $I_d$ in a parallel plate capacitor is defined as the current flowing through the circuit, which is equal to the conduction current $I_c$ in the connecting wires.

The relationship between the conduction current and the displacement current is given by $I_d = I_c$.

Given that the rms value of the current in the circuit is $I_{rms} = 4 \mu \text{A}$, this current represents the conduction current flowing through the wires connected to the capacitor plates.

According to the principle of continuity of current, the displacement current between the plates of the capacitor must be equal to the conduction current in the external circuit.

Therefore, $I_d = I_{rms} = 4 \mu \text{A}$.

Answer: 4 $\mu$ A

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A parallel plate capacitor is filled by a dielectric whose relative permittivity varies with the applied voltage (U) as $\epsilon=2 U$. A similar capacitor with no dielectric is charged to $U_0=78 \mathrm{ V}$. It is then connected to the uncharged capacitor with the dielectric. Find the final voltage on the capacitors.
questions.solution:
Let $C_0$ be the capacitance of the capacitor without the dielectric. The charge on this capacitor is $Q_0 = C_0 U_0$, where $U_0 = 78$ V.

When the two capacitors are connected in parallel, the total charge $Q_0$ is shared between them. Let $U$ be the final common voltage. The charge on the first capacitor is $Q_1 = C_0 U$.

The second capacitor has a dielectric with relative permittivity $\epsilon = 2U$. The capacitance of this capacitor is $C = \epsilon C_0 = (2U) C_0$. The charge on this capacitor is $Q_2 = C U = (2U) C_0 U = 2 C_0 U^2$.

By the principle of conservation of charge, $Q_0 = Q_1 + Q_2$.

$C_0 U_0 = C_0 U + 2 C_0 U^2$.

Dividing by $C_0$, we get $U_0 = U + 2U^2$.

Substituting $U_0 = 78$, we have $2U^2 + U - 78 = 0$.

Solving the quadratic equation for $U$ using the quadratic formula $U = \dfrac{-b \pm \sqrt{b^2 - 4ac}}{2a}$:

$U = \dfrac{-1 \pm \sqrt{1^2 - 4(2)(-78)}}{2(2)} = \dfrac{-1 \pm \sqrt{1 + 624}}{4} = \dfrac{-1 \pm \sqrt{625}}{4} = \dfrac{-1 \pm 25}{4}$.

Since voltage must be positive, $U = \dfrac{24}{4} = 6$ V.

Answer: 6V

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A capacitor of capacity $2 \mu \mathrm{F}$ is charged upto a potential $14 \mathrm{ V}$ and then connected in parallel to an uncharged capacitor of capacity $5 \mu \mathrm{F}$. The final potential difference across each capacitor will be
questions.solution:
$When two capacitors are connected then their common potential difference is
\begin{aligned} V=\frac{C_1 V_1+C_2 V_2}{C_1+C_2} \\
\text{ Given, } C_1 & =2 \mu \mathrm{F}, V_1=14 \mathrm{ V}, C_2=5 \mu \mathrm{F}, V_2=0 \mathrm{ V} \\
\therefore \quad V=\frac{2 \times 14+5 \times 0}{2+5}=4 \mathrm{ V}
\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A dielectric of dielectric constant $K$ is introduced such that half of its area of a capacitor of capacitance $C$ is occupied by it. The new capacity is
questions.solution:
The dielectric is introduced such that half of its area is occupied by it. In the given case, the two capacitors are in parallel.
$\therefore \quad C^{\prime}=C_1+C_2$ But $\quad C_1=\frac{A \varepsilon_0}{2 d}$ and $C_2=\frac{K A \varepsilon_0}{2 d}$ Thus, $\quad C^{\prime}=\frac{A \varepsilon_0}{2 d}+\frac{K A \varepsilon_0}{2 d} \Rightarrow C^{\prime}=\frac{C}{2}(1+K)$

questions.q: In the figure below, the capacitance of each capacitor is $3 \mu \mathrm{F}$. The effective capacitance between $A$ and $B$ is
questions.solution:
From figure,
$C_1=C_2=C_3=C_4=3 \mu \mathrm{F} \quad (given)\because C_4$ and $C_3$ are in parallel, i.e. $C_{\text{eq }}=C_4+C_3=(3+3) \mu \mathrm{F}=6 \mu \mathrm{F}$ Now arrangement of capacitors will be as follows
$\because C_1$ is in parallel with the series combination of $C_2$ and $C_{\text{eq }}^{\prime}$. $\therefore C_{\text{eq }}^{\prime \prime}$ between $A$ and $B=\frac{\left(C_2 \times C_{\mathrm{eq}^{\prime}\right)}{C_2+C_{\mathrm{eq}^{\prime}}+C_1 \Rightarrow\left(\frac{3 \times 6}{3+6}\right)+3=5 \mu \mathrm{F}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: In the figure, first the capacitors are fully charged by closing the key $\mathrm{K}$. Then after opening the Key a dielectric material with dielectric constant 2 is filled in the space between the plates of both the capacitor. At this state the ratio of the Charge on the capacitor $C_1$ to that of $C_2$ is:
questions.solution:
When key K is closed, both $C_1$ and $C_2$ ($= 1\ \mu F$ each) are connected to the 12V battery. Initial charge on both:
$Q_1 = Q_2 = 1\ \mu F \times 12\ V = 12\ \mu C$

When key K is opened, $C_2$ gets isolated — its charge stays constant at $12\ \mu C$. $C_1$ remains connected to the battery.

Dielectric with $k = 2$ is inserted in both. New capacitances: $C_1' = C_2' = 2\ \mu F$

For $C_1$ (still connected to battery, $V = 12\ V$):
$Q_1' = 2\ \mu F \times 12\ V = 24\ \mu C$

For $C_2$ (isolated, charge conserved):
$Q_2' = 12\ \mu C$

$\dfrac{Q_1'}{Q_2'} = \dfrac{24}{12} = \dfrac{2}{1}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: If $C$ be the capacitance and $V$ be the electric potential, then the dimensional formula of $\mathrm{CV}^2$ is
questions.solution:
The energy $U$ stored in a capacitor is given by the formula $U = \dfrac{1}{2} CV^2$.

Since $U$ represents energy, its dimensional formula is the same as that of work or energy, which is $[ML^2T^{-2}]$.

The factor $\dfrac{1}{2}$ is a dimensionless constant and does not affect the dimensions.

Therefore, the dimensional formula of $CV^2$ is the same as the dimensional formula of energy, which is $[ML^2T^{-2}A^0]$.

Answer: $\left[\mathrm{ML}^2 \mathrm{~T}^{-2} \mathrm{~A}^0\right]$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A dielectric of dielectric constant $K$ is introduced such that half of its area of a capacitor of capacitance $C$ is occupied by it. The new capacity is
questions.solution:
The initial capacitance of the parallel plate capacitor is $C = \dfrac{\epsilon_0 A}{d}$, where $A$ is the area of the plates and $d$ is the distance between them.

When a dielectric of dielectric constant $K$ is introduced such that it occupies half the area, the capacitor can be viewed as two capacitors connected in parallel. One capacitor has area $A/2$ with air (dielectric constant 1) and the other has area $A/2$ with the dielectric (dielectric constant $K$).

The capacitance of the air-filled part is $C_1 = \dfrac{\epsilon_0 (A/2)}{d} = \dfrac{C}{2}$.

The capacitance of the dielectric-filled part is $C_2 = \dfrac{K \epsilon_0 (A/2)}{d} = \dfrac{KC}{2}$.

Since these are in parallel, the total capacitance is $C_{new} = C_1 + C_2 = \dfrac{C}{2} + \dfrac{KC}{2} = \dfrac{C(1+K)}{2}$.

Answer: $\dfrac{(1+K) C}{2}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A capacitor of capacity $2 \mu \mathrm{F}$ is charged upto a potential $14 \mathrm{ V}$ and then connected in parallel to an uncharged capacitor of capacity $5 \mu \mathrm{F}$. The final potential difference across each capacitor will be
questions.solution:
The initial charge $Q$ on the first capacitor is given by $Q = C_1 V_1$.

$Q = 2 \mu \text{F} \times 14 \text{V} = 28 \mu \text{C}$.

When the two capacitors are connected in parallel, the total charge $Q$ is conserved and is shared between the two capacitors. Let $V$ be the common potential difference across the capacitors.

$Q = (C_1 + C_2) V$.

Substituting the given values:

$28 \mu \text{C} = (2 \mu \text{F} + 5 \mu \text{F}) \times V$.

$28 = 7 \times V$.

$V = \dfrac{28}{7} \text{V} = 4 \text{V}$.

Answer: 4 V

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: In the figure below, the capacitance of each capacitor is $3 \mu \mathrm{F}$. The effective capacitance between $A$ and $B$ is
questions.solution:
Let M be the intermediate node between the two middle capacitors.

Between A and M: top capacitor and left-middle capacitor are in parallel:
$C_{AM} = 3 + 3 = 6\ \mu F$

Between M and B: right-middle capacitor and bottom capacitor are in parallel:
$C_{MB} = 3 + 3 = 6\ \mu F$

$C_{AM}$ and $C_{MB}$ are in series:

$\dfrac{1}{C_{AB}} = \dfrac{1}{6} + \dfrac{1}{6} = \dfrac{2}{6} = \dfrac{1}{3}$

$C_{AB} = 3\ \mu F$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: In the network shown in figure, the equivalent capacitance between points $P$ and $Q$ is
questions.solution:
Simplify from right to left.

Rightmost section: $3\mu F$, $3\mu F$, $3\mu F$ in series (path $B \to C \to D \to E$):
$\dfrac{1}{C_{eq1}} = \dfrac{1}{3} + \dfrac{1}{3} + \dfrac{1}{3} = 1 \Rightarrow C_{eq1} = 1\mu F$

This $1\mu F$ is in parallel with $2\mu F$ (between $B$ and $E$):
$C_{BE} = 1 + 2 = 3\mu F$

Next section: $3\mu F$, $3\mu F$ ($C_{BE}$), $3\mu F$ in series (path $A \to B \to E \to F$):
$\dfrac{1}{C_{eq2}} = \dfrac{1}{3} + \dfrac{1}{3} + \dfrac{1}{3} = 1 \Rightarrow C_{eq2} = 1\mu F$

This $1\mu F$ is in parallel with $2\mu F$ (between $A$ and $F$):
$C_{AF} = 1 + 2 = 3\mu F$

Final section: $3\mu F$ (at $P$), $3\mu F$ ($C_{AF}$), $3\mu F$ (at $Q$) in series:
$\dfrac{1}{C_{PQ}} = \dfrac{1}{3} + \dfrac{1}{3} + \dfrac{1}{3} = 1 \Rightarrow C_{PQ} = 1\mu F$

Correct option: (1)

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The formula of capacitative reactance is
questions.solution:
The capacitive reactance $X_{C}$ of a capacitor in an alternating current circuit is defined as the opposition offered by the capacitor to the flow of alternating current.

The formula for capacitive reactance is given by $X_{C} = \dfrac{1}{\omega C}$, where $\omega$ is the angular frequency of the AC source and $C$ is the capacitance.

Since the angular frequency $\omega$ is related to the frequency $f$ by the relation $\omega = 2 \pi f$, substituting this into the expression for $X_{C}$ yields $X_{C} = \dfrac{1}{2 \pi f C}$.

Answer: $\dfrac{1}{2 \pi f C}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A spherical drop of capacitance $1 \mu \mathrm{F}$ is broken into eight drops of equal radius. Then, the capacitance of each small drop is
questions.solution:
Given, capacitance of bigger drop $=1 \mu \mathrm{F}$
Let $R$ be the radius of bigger drop and $r$ be the radius of smaller drops.
According to the question, $\frac{4}{3} \pi R^{3}=8 \times \frac{4}{3} \pi r^{3} \begin{aligned}
\Rightarrow& R^{3}=8 r^{3} \\
\Rightarrow & R=2 r^{2}
\end{aligned} The capacitance of bigger drop , \begin{aligned} C &=4 \pi \varepsilon_{0} R \\
&=2 \times4 \pi \varepsilon_{0} r \quad(\because R=2 r)
\end{aligned} Capacitance of smaller drop, $ C^{\prime}=4 \pi \varepsilon_{0} r$
Thus, \begin{aligned} C^{\prime} &=\frac{C}{2}\\
C^{\prime} &=\frac{1}{2} \mu \mathrm{F}
\end{aligned}$ Hence,
$C^{\prime}=\frac{1}{2} \mu \mathrm{F}$

questions.q: How many $6 \mu \mathrm{F}, 200 \mathrm{ V}$ condensers are needed to make a condenser of $18 \mu \mathrm{F}, 600 \mathrm{ V}$ ?\
questions.solution:
We know that, in series combination of capacitors, net potential difference is equal to sum of the individual potential difference of each capacitor
i.e., $V=V_{1}+V_{2}+V_{3} \ldots . . \quad\left[V_{1}=V_{2}=V_{3}=200 \mathrm{ V}\right]\Rightarrow 600=n \times 200\Rightarrow \quad n=3$
So, there should be 3 capacitors in series to obtain the required potential difference. The equivalent capacitance of 3 capacitors in series is given as $\frac{1}{C_{\text{eq }}}=\frac{1}{6}+\frac{1}{6}+\frac{1}{6}=\frac{3}{6}=\frac{1}{2}\Rightarrow \quad C_{\text{eq }}=2 \mu \mathrm{F}  Now, we require $18 \mu $\mathrm{u}$ capacitance for this, we need 9 number of such capacitors in parallel. $\therefore$ Total number of capacitors (condensers) $=9 \times 3=27 9 number of such capacitors in parallel.
$\therefore$ Total number of capacitors (condensers)$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: An air filled parallel plate condenser has a capacity of $2 \mathrm{pF}$. The separation of the plates is doubled and the interspace between the plates is filled with wax. If the capacity is increased to $6 \mathrm{pF}$, then the dielectric constant of wax is
questions.solution:
Given, capacitance of air filled parallel plate capacitor,
$C_{0}=2 \mathrm{pF}\Rightarrow \quad=2 \times 10^{-12} \mathrm{ F}\Rightarrow \quad \frac{\varepsilon_{0} A}{d}=2 \times 10^{-12} \mathrm{ F}...(i)$
When the separation between the plates is doubled, i.e., $\quad d^{\prime}=2 d$
And wax of dielectric constant $k$ is filled between the plates of capacitor, then,
$\begin{aligned}
C^{\prime} &=6 \mathrm{pF} \\
\frac{\varepsilon_{0} k A}{d^{\prime}} &=6 \times 10^{-12} \mathrm{ F}
\end{aligned}\Rightarrow \quad \frac{\varepsilon_{0} k A}{2 d}=6 \times 10^{-12} \quad\left[\because d^{\prime}=2 d\right]\Rightarrow \quad \frac{\varepsilon_{0} A}{d} \times \frac{k}{2}=6 \times 10^{-12}\Rightarrow 2 \times 10^{-12} \times \frac{k}{2}=6 \times 10^{-12}$
[from $\mathrm{Eq} .$ (i)]
$\Rightarrow \quad k=6$

questions.q: A metal plate of thickness $d / 2$ is introduced in between the plates of a parallel plate air capacitor with plate separation of $d$, then capacity
questions.solution:
Given, $t=\frac{d}{2}$
The capacitance is given by
$C=\frac{\varepsilon_{0} A}{d}$
For dielectric medium between plates,
$C^{\prime}=\frac{\varepsilon_{0} A}{d-t+\frac{t}{K}}$
For metal, $K=$ infinity
$\Rightarrow \quad C^{\prime}=\frac{\varepsilon_{0} A}{d-\frac{d}{2}}=\frac{2 \varepsilon_{0} A}{d}=2 C$
Hence, capacitance increases 2 times.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Three identical capacitors are first connected in series and then in parallel. The ratio of effective capacitances in the two cases is
questions.solution:
The equivalent capacitance of three capacitors connected in series is given by
$\frac{1}{C_{s}}=\frac{1}{C_{1}}+\frac{1}{C_{2}}+\frac{1}{C_{3}}$
Given, $C_{1}=C_{2}=C_{3}=C\frac{1}{C_{s}}=\frac{3}{C} \text{ or } C_{s}=\frac{C}{3}$
Similarly, for parallel combination,
$C_{p}=C+C+C=3 C\therefore$ Ratio of equivalent capacitance,
$\frac{C_{s}}{C_{p}}=\frac{C / 3}{3 C}=\frac{1}{9} \text{ or } 1: 9$

questions.q: A parallel plate capacitor has a capacity $C$. The separation between the plates is doubled and a dielectric medium is inserted between the plates. If the capacity is $3 C$, then the dielectric constant of the medium will be
questions.solution:
We know that, capacitance of a parallel plate capacitor, C=$\frac{\varepsilon_{0} A}{d}$ where, $A=$ area of plate
$d=$ separation between the plates.
When $d^{\prime}=2 d$, then
$C^{\prime}=\frac{\varepsilon_{0} A K}{d^{\prime}}\Rightarrow \quad 3 C=\frac{\varepsilon_{0} A K}{2 d}\left[\because C^{\prime}=3 C\right]\Rightarrow \quad 3 C=\frac{\varepsilon_{0} A}{d} \cdot \frac{K}{2}\Rightarrow \quad 3 C=C \cdot \frac{K}{2} \quad$ [from Eq. (i)]
$\Rightarrow \quad 3=\frac{K}{2}\Rightarrow \quad K=6$

questions.q: A $10 \mathrm{mF}$ capacitor has been charged to a potential of $100 \mathrm{ V}$. Suddenly if it explodes, the energy given out is
questions.solution:
Given, capacitance, $C=10 \mathrm{mF}=10^{-2} \mathrm{~F}$
Potential, $V=100 \mathrm{~V}$
When capacitor explodes, then its whole stored potential energy is given out in the form of heat and lightning.

\therefore \quad E_{$\text{out }$}=$\frac{1}{2}$C V^{2}=$\frac{1}{2} \times$10^{-2} $\times($100)^{2}=50 $\mathrm{~J}$

questions.q: A $10 \mu \mathrm{F}$ capacitor is charged to $10 \mathrm{ V}$ and disconnected from the battery. If another uncharged $10 \mu \mathrm{F}$ capacitor is connected across it in parallel, then the voltage across the combination will be
questions.solution:
Common potential difference for a parallel combination of capacitors, is
$V_{C}=\frac{V_{1} C_{1}+V_{2} C_{2}}{C_{1}+C_{2}}$
Given, $\begin{aligned} V_{2} &=0, V_{1}=10 \mathrm{ V}\\
C_{1} &=C_{2}=10 \mu \mathrm{F}=10 \times10^{-6} \mathrm{ F}
\end{aligned}\begin{aligned} \therefore \quad V_{C} &=\frac{10 \times 10 \times 10^{-6}}{(10+10) \times 10^{-6}} \\ &=\frac{100}{20}=5 \mathrm{ V} \end{aligned}$
